title: The Dental Assistant, Pillar of the Practice
subtitle: Dr Chiba & Dr Zaki Count on You
synopsis:
Welcome, Doctor! 

Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki are two passionate dentists. One hired an assistant trained "on the job," the other chose a DUT-trained Dental Assistant.

But a crucial question arises: does the assistant's training really make a difference?

Between hygiene, sterilization, stock management, emergencies, management software and patient relations… the stakes are high.

A bad recruitment, insufficient training, and patient safety is threatened. 

The quality of care, the practice's reputation, and peace of mind rest on YOUR shoulders.

chapters.debutant1: The Dental Assistant, Pillar of the Practice - Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki are two passionate dentists. One hired an assistant trained 'on the job,' the other chose a DUT-trained Dental Assistant. But a crucial question arises: does the assistant's training really make a difference?
chapters.debutant2: The Foundations of the Profession - Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki deepen their reflection on the role of the assistant. They discover that DUT training covers essential areas: hygiene, sterilization, stock management, emergencies and patient relations.
chapters.intermediaire1: Recruitment and Training - Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki need to recruit new assistants. They compare approaches: experience vs diploma, on-the-job training vs structured training. The choice commits the future of the practice.
chapters.intermediaire2: Emergency Management - Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki face emergency situations. The assistant plays a key role in crisis management. Her training and responsiveness make the difference.
chapters.expert1: Communication and Patient Relations - Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki become experts in team management. They train their assistants in communication, conflict management and patient relations.
chapters.expert2: Excellence and Succession - After years of collaboration, Dr Chiba and Dr Zaki have formed an exceptional team. They pass on their knowledge to the new generation. The assistant is recognized as an indispensable pillar of the practice.
